root_cause.text: The Intel uncore discovery code parsed PCI discovery tables for dies with no online CPUs and failed to validate that the die ID returned by get_device_die_id() was within uncore_max_dies(), allowing uncore_pci_pmu_register() to index pmu->boxes[die] out of bounds.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that “the discovery table continues to be parsed even if all CPUs in the associated die are offline” and this “can lead to an array overflow at ‘pmu->boxes[die] = box’”; the patch fixes this by changing the check from only `if (die < 0)` to `if ((die < 0) || (die >= uncore_max_dies())) continue;` before `parse_discovery_table(...)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an upper-bound validation for die IDs in uncore discovery so invalid die indices are skipped before parsing.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding use of the die ID in uncore_discovery_pci() was changed from checking only `die < 0` to checking both `die < 0` and `die >= uncore_max_dies()`, causing the loop to continue when the die index is negative or exceeds the maximum valid die count.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents parse_discovery_table() from being called with an out-of-range die index, avoiding invalid access or incorrect per-die uncore discovery processing for devices that report a die ID outside the supported range.

grouping_result.intent: Add an upper-bound validation for die IDs in uncore discovery so invalid die indices are skipped before parsing.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause by adding an upper-bound check on die IDs during uncore discovery, preventing invalid die indices from being used and avoiding out-of-bounds access to pmu->boxes[die].

candidates.rationale: This call propagates an unvalidated die index into discovery parsing, which later leads to uncore_pci_pmu_register() indexing pmu->boxes[die] out of bounds. The missing upper-bound check before this statement is the core flaw.

The die value obtained here may be invalid for systems with no online CPUs on a die. Because only negative values were rejected, an out-of-range positive die ID could flow onward and trigger out-of-bounds indexing.
This check is insufficient because it rejects only negative die IDs and fails to enforce the required upper bound against uncore_max_dies(), allowing invalid positive die indices to pass.

vuln_statements.explanation: This validation was incomplete: it rejected only negative die IDs and did not verify that the positive die ID was less than uncore_max_dies(). As a result, invalid out-of-range die values could continue into discovery parsing and later cause out-of-bounds indexing of pmu->boxes[die].

This statement consumed the unvalidated die value and propagated it into the discovery path. Because the preceding check lacked an upper-bound validation, an out-of-range die index could reach later registration code and trigger the out-of-bounds access.

This statement retrieved the die ID that could be invalid on systems with dies lacking online CPUs. The vulnerability arose because the returned value was not subsequently validated against the maximum allowed die index before use.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full die-ID derivation and use path in the newly introduced discovery logic. The root cause is missing validation that the die returned by get_device_die_id() is within the maximum number of uncore dies. That vulnerable construct is present here. Specifically, `get_device_die_id()` can return `c->logical_die_id` for a CPU on the node, or `-1` if all CPUs are offline. In `intel_uncore_has_discovery_tables()`, the code does `die = get_device_die_id(dev);` and only checks `if (die < 0) continue;` before calling `parse_discovery_table(dev, die, bar_offset, &parsed);`. There is no upper-bound check such as `die >= uncore_max_dies()` or equivalent. The `die` value is then used as an array index in `uncore_insert_box_info()`, e.g. `if (!type->box_ctrl_die[die]) type->box_ctrl_die[die] = unit->ctl;` and `type->box_ctrl_die[die] = unit->ctl;`. Since `box_ctrl_die` is allocated with `kcalloc(__uncore_max_dies, sizeof(u64), GFP_KERNEL);`, using an unchecked die value larger than the allocated number of dies can lead to out-of-bounds access. The commit message and code also explicitly handle cases where some dies may not have online CPUs (`All CPUs of a node may be offlined`), which matches the vulnerability scenario. Therefore the bug is present, and the fix is not yet present because only `die < 0` is checked, with no validation against the maximum die count.
